land.text: Kuwait, a British protectorate (Anglo-Kuwaiti Agreement of 23 January 1899)

predecessors.note: The United Kingdom is the protecting power; the eu-11 group is to create the 'United Kingdom' slug for the years after 1800, which should replace this one. Kuwait itself is older: Cliopatria's 'Kuwait' row (1757-1872) is the same state.

land.text: Kuwait restored on the end of the Iraqi occupation, 26 February 1991

successors.note: The same state (Wikidata Q817): the Cliopatria row 'Kuwait' resumes in 1991 after the Iraqi occupation of 1990.

capitals.name: Kuwait City
capitals.note: The Kuwait page: 'Capital and largest city: Kuwait City'.

correction.text: unchanged: Kuwait without the neutral zone; holds 1961 to 1965 only

keyframe_review.note: 1961-1972, 14,031 km2 against the Kuwait infobox's 17,818 km2 (ratio 0.79, within a factor of two): Kuwait without its half of the Saudi-Kuwaiti neutral zone, which was shared until the partition 'took effect on 25 July 1966'. So the shape is right for 1961-1965 only; from July 1966 see the 1973 shape. The 50 cells are 20 fewer than Natural Earth's Kuwait: 13 are the neutral-zone half, the rest coastline and border noise.

correction.text: unchanged: Kuwait with its share of the former neutral zone; holds from July 1966 to 1986, not from 1973

keyframe_review.note: 1973-1986, 17,395 km2 against 17,818 km2 (ratio 0.98): Kuwait with its share of the former neutral zone, 13 cells at about 28.6-29.0 N, 47.7-48.4 E that the 1961 shape lacks. The partition took effect on 25 July 1966 (agreement of 7 July 1965); the demarcation agreement signed on 17 December 1967 took formal effect on 18 December 1969 and was ratified on 18 January 1970. So the shape holds from 1966, not 1973. The 62 cells are 8 fewer than Natural Earth's Kuwait (the northern border strip), which Cliopatria does not change after the 1993 UN demarcation either.
1987-1989, the same 62 cells and 17,395 km2 as 1973-1986. Nothing on the Kuwait page moves a border before 2 August 1990.

correction.text: Kuwait, the whole state, under Iraqi occupation from 2 August 1990

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1990: Cliopatria has no Kuwait row for 1990 and draws the whole of Kuwait inside the Iraqi shape ('In August 1990, Iraqi forces invaded and annexed Kuwait'). Kuwait remains the owner and is hatched as occupied land until 26 February 1991 (rule 4); the Iraqi dossier cuts Kuwait out of its own 1990 shape. The 1991 row (kuwait) takes over for the whole of 1991.

ledger.note: 19 June 1961: Kuwait becomes independent from Britain. Infobox 'Independence from the United Kingdom: 19 June 1961'; 'In June 1961, Kuwait became independent with the end of the British protectorate'; the Anglo-Kuwaiti Agreement of 23 January 1899 'gave Britain exclusive access and trade with Kuwait'. Iraq 'initially refused to recognize the country's independence by maintaining that Kuwait is part of Iraq'.

region.text: Kuwait's share of the neutral zone, as the 13 cells Cliopatria adds in 1973; the page does not say how the zone was divided

ledger.note: 25 July 1966: Kuwait takes its half of the Saudi-Kuwaiti neutral zone. 'On 7 July 1965, the two governments signed an agreement to partition the zone (which took effect on 25 July 1966)'; the demarcation agreement signed on 17 December 1967 took formal effect on 18 December 1969 and was ratified on 18 January 1970. The zone, 5,770 km2, had been left undefined by the Uqair Convention of 2 December 1922 with equal rights for both sides; the page does not say how it was split, so the region is the cells Cliopatria adds between its 1961 and 1973 shapes. Reviewer me-10-k (2026-10-25): counterpart changed from kingdom-of-saudi-arabia to nobody: the zone was shared, not Saudi land ('the Government of Najd and Kuwait will share equal rights', Uqair Convention, on the neutral-zone page), neither state's Cliopatria shape held it before the partition, and the Saudi-Iraqi zone of 1982 is entered with counterpart nobody on both sides.

2 August 1990: Iraq invades Kuwait. Infobox 'Iraqi invasion of Kuwait: 2 August 1990'; 'In August 1990, Iraqi forces invaded and annexed Kuwait without any warning'. The annexation was never recognised, so Kuwait is drawn as occupied land, not as Iraqi.

26 February 1991: the Iraqi occupation of Kuwait ends. 'The Iraqi occupation of Kuwait ended on 26 February 1991' (the infobox gives 'Liberation of Kuwait: 28 February 1991'); Kuwait 'celebrates 26 February as Liberation Day'.

1991: Cliopatria's State of Kuwait row ends and its Kuwait row resumes in 1991 over the same cells. Not the end of a state: a row boundary that the page does not date, bridged by the researcher (the end date follows the liberation of 26 February 1991).

wars.name: Kuwait crisis of 1961 (Operation Vantage)
wars.outcome: Iraq threatened to invade in July 1961 and did not: the invasion 'was finally averted following plans by the Arab League to form an international Arab force'; British forces had withdrawn by 19 October and the Arab League took over border security. In 1963 Iraq recognised 'the 1932 border of Kuwait' by a treaty of friendship.
wars.note: A threat, not a campaign: no ground was taken or held, so no contest event.

wars.name: Invasion of Kuwait and Gulf War

zones.text: the whole of Kuwait, invaded 2 August 1990, liberated 26 February 1991

wars.outcome: Iraq invaded and annexed Kuwait on 2 August 1990; the occupation ended on 26 February 1991.
wars.note: The Kuwait page does not name the coalition; the Iraq page calls it 'US-led'.

certainty.note: Frontiers follow the 1922 Uqair Convention lines with Saudi Arabia and the 1932 line with Iraq, which Iraq accepted in the 1963 treaty. Exceptions: the neutral zone, shared and undefined until its partition took effect in July 1966 (soft to 1965), and the occupied year 1990-1991.

notes: Written by me-10-k on 2026-10-25 from two pages (plus the Kuwait-Saudi border page, opened first, which said only 'agreed to partition it in 1965 ... ratified in 1969-70' and is replaced by the neutral-zone page). SAME STATE AS 'kuwait': 'State of Kuwait' (1961-1989) and 'Kuwait' (1757-1872, 1991-2024) share Wikidata Q817 and are one state with Cliopatria rows missing for 1873-1960 (British protectorate) and 1990 (Iraqi occupation). The earlier slug is 'kuwait', written by another part (me-10-d); I kept this one separate because the brief owns it, so the two dossiers must be joined by the colour agent (colours.json gives them different hues, #ca933e and #b85e31) or by a final merge. The ending in February 1991 is a row boundary, not a dissolution; 1991 is shared with the 'kuwait' row, whose shape governs the whole year. DECISION: the Iraqi invasion is recorded as occupation (hatched) rather than as an Iraqi gain, because the annexation was never recognised; the Iraqi dossier does the same and cuts Kuwait out of its 1990 shape. DISAGREEMENT: the Saudi dossier (another group) dates the neutral-zone partition 25 July 1966 with counterpart 'kuwait'; this one uses the same date and counterpart 'kingdom-of-saudi-arabia' for the Kuwaiti side. Not opened (page budget): the 1993 UN Iraq-Kuwait boundary demarcation, which the Iraq-Kuwait border page only calls 'the 1932 line with some minor adjustments' and which Cliopatria does not show; the Bubiyan and Warbah islands, which that page says Britain confirmed as Kuwaiti in 1932. Rulers not entered: the Kuwait page does not date Abdullah III (1950-1965) or Sabah III (1965-1977).
